body.text: Xi’s visit prolongs a pause in the trade war at least until January. This truce appears to be more important for Trump, who faces the November midterm elections and reportedly has no plan how to end the protracted war with Iran. Xi, meantime, appears confident in his ability to use economic coercion against Washington, if necessary.

Xi gave pompous speeches, for example “about working with President Trump to steer the great ship of China-US relations toward steady and sustained progress”, and about offering two giant pandas to the US “as ambassadors of friendship between the two countries”.
However, these speeches masked his hard-hitting message to Trump.

Xi sought to leave an impression during every opportunity to demonstrate China’s superiority over the United States. And Trump helped him with this. China immediately published Xi’s entire remarks (in the White House , and over dinner ), including his talks with Trump , while the Trump administration only released a brief summary after Xi left Washington, giving Chinese leader the upper hand in the narrative tug-of-war.
Posing for a photo on the West Colonnade overlooking the White House Rose Garden 24 September 2026 (Molly Riley/Official White House Photo)
Xi’s real message to Trump operated on multiple levels.

China’s president repeatedly stated that both countries are superpowers – and while that message was not new, saying it in Washington without even the slightest challenge from his host was remarkable.

Xi also described China and the United States as great powers in AI and should therefore take responsibility for managing artificial intelligence to ensure people’s safety. Trump dismisses threats from AI as a hoax , ceding Xi an advantage in terms of public perception. Never mind what Xi really intended when he spoke about controlling AI – Beijing has been training its LLM models according to its own ideology .

Xi also reminded Trump that China had coined the term “ constructive relationship with strategic stability ” to describe US–China relations. China was pleased that Trump had accepted this term when he visited Beijing in May and this same slogan appeared in a White House communiqué . In short, Xi illustrated China’s ability to exercise power over the discourse . And it does not matter that no one yet knows what this slogan means.

Even Xi’s use of historical examples appeared intended to demonstrate China’s superiority in terms of culture, science and craftsmanship between China and the United States – referring to revolutionary leader George Washington’s collection of Chinese porcelain, citing a history of trade reaching back more than 200 years to the beginning of US independence. He spoke of Chinese soldiers rescuing American pilots 80 years ago during the war with Japan via a dangerous air corridor over the Himalayas (known as the Hump Route ) but ignored US support to China at the same time. And Xi’s focus on ping-pong diplomacy in the 1970s and praise for the “political wisdom” of Mao and Nixon could be interpreted as an appeal to Trump to be wiser and more predictable.

Xi did not hesitate to mention China’s red lines , such as opposing Taiwanese independence. He also expressed (diplomatically) his anger that Chinese companies are not treated fairly by the United States. The implication was that Trump’s foreign policy agenda makes a list of global problems longer instead of shortening it.
Although a display of pomp, Xi seized the opportunity to promote his own agenda. And in this narrative battle, Xi has emerged the winner.
